items.title: As AI Closed In on 'Unique Games' Proof, Researchers Raced to Beat the Machines
items.excerpt: In the shadow of a rumored AI proof of one of the biggest problems in their field, three computer scientists rushed to publish their own milestone result.
items.rationale: A new milestone result on the Unique Games conjecture, published early because an AI proof was rumored to be close. This is a different problem and event from the earlier Millennium Prize, sphere-packing and probability cards.

items.title: New AI method uses engineering knowledge to estimate disaster damage from incomplete satellite imagery
items.excerpt: A new technology has been developed that can rapidly predict city-scale structural damage even when portions of satellite imagery are obscured by clouds or smoke immediately after a disaster. The method folds engineering knowledge into the model so missing pixels do not break the estimate.
items.rationale: A new physics-informed method that estimates city-scale structural damage after a disaster when the imagery is obscured. It is post-event damage assessment, which is a different study from the 09-13 forecasting feature and the 10-07 flash-flood card.

items.title: Open-sourcing AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model in Asta
items.excerpt: Ai2 is releasing AstaBrief, an 8B open-weights model for generating cited scientific reports, available in Asta's Fast mode or to download and run on your own infrastructure.
items.rationale: A primary-source release of an 8B open-weights model that writes cited scientific reports. Researchers can run it themselves, and it is unrelated to the 09-08 Ai2 BenchMIRT card.

items.title: Haiqu Releases AgenticOS to Plan and Check Quantum Research
items.excerpt: Haiqu launched AgenticOS, a system that coordinates specialized AI agents to plan, validate and prepare quantum research experiments.
items.rationale: A new product release in which coordinated AI agents plan and validate quantum experiments. It comes from a different company and does something different from the earlier IonQ, QC Design and MIT optics-lab quantum cards.

items.title: New Calibration Framework Improves Confidence in AI Virtual Cell Models
items.source: GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News
items.excerpt: Metrics such as mean squared error and control-referenced Pearson correlation are frequently miscalibrated when used to judge AI virtual cell models, according to the authors, who propose a calibration framework instead.
items.rationale: A new framework for evaluating AI virtual cell models, showing that the standard metrics (MSE, control-referenced Pearson) are miscalibrated. It is an AI-evaluation result, not one of the earlier virtual-cell model releases (09-24, 09-15), and it is basic biology rather than clinical, so it stays in science. It also adds GEN as a fifth outlet.

dedup.note: None of the 22 candidates repeats a story from the 30-day history. All 6 history_match tags are in the 'related' band, and each points to a different study. SWAP PASS: the Phys.org spatial-transcriptomics pick (https://phys.org/news/2026-10-algorithm-gene-easier-cell.html) was removed after fact-check. Its Domain Elastic Transform method is a training-free, non-ML registration algorithm, so it is not an AI story. It was replaced by GEN's AI virtual-cell calibration framework. That candidate's history_match points to the 09-13 Psychology Today 'AI Behavior Impacted by Internal Confidence Levels' card (related band, a different topic: LLM confidence vs. cell-model metrics). The closer published story is the 09-24 Phys.org 'Virtual cells built from 4D AI models' card. That card was a model-building study, while this is a new evaluation and calibration framework, so it is a separate event and the verdict is new. It is also distinct from the 09-15 Stanford cross-species cell models and the 09-22 cell-type comparison tool. There is no overlap with today's medicine picks (pediatric bone age FDA, Teladoc, Parkinson's telerehab RCT, Clairity, Swiss radiology AI study). Alternates considered for the swap: Ai2 Bolmo is a Nature publication of an already-released language-model technique, would be a second Ai2 card, and is not a science application. GEN hybrid digital twins is mechanistic modelling plus AI, so it is less AI-centred. GEN low-fidelity data is a narrower bioprocess-modelling result. The Tech Xplore spiking-network study would be a second Tech Xplore card and is computational neuroscience. NOT PICKED on safety or section-boundary grounds: (1) DeepMind SynthID Bio was skipped on the biosecurity-adjacent rule; it has no og_image either. (2) Phys.org MALVINA (bacterial invasion of human cells) was skipped as pathogen-adjacent. (3) The bioRxiv preprint testing AlphaGenome on ALS was skipped because it names a specific disease, so it leans toward medicine; it also continues the AlphaGenome story published 09-09 and 09-20. NOT PICKED as essays or explainers: Quanta 'Is AI the End of Math', MIT Technology Review's LLM-reasoning opinion piece, SciAm on attachment theory, SciAm on distillation (industry dispute), and the Tech Xplore lie-detector expert piece. Physics World's wildlife-drones feature is evergreen and overlaps the 10-03 Antarctica drones card. In the SciAm Etruscan tomb story the AI role is unclear. RGI-Toolkit has no og_image. The 5 picks come from 5 different outlets: Quanta, Tech Xplore, Ai2, The Quantum Insider and GEN.
